title: Close deterministic rule-procedure implementation gaps (engine epic F1-F10)
description: Home for the engine-side implementation work identified by the eshyra-o9bd.18.7.8 execution-boundary classification (docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/2026-07-06-o9bd-18-7-8-execution-boundary-classification.md, §4). That artifact found 21 implementation-required + 47 partial deterministic rule procedures clustering into ten shared-primitive families (F1 dice-grammar, F2 action-economy budget, F3 concentration/active-effects, F4 spell-slot economy, F5 usage/recharge/attunement, F6 death/dying/HP-buffer, F7 rest engine, F8 character-build gap closures, F9 derived-math primitives, F10 currency surface), plus two design decisions (D1 multiclass scope, D2 creation-variant policy). These are engine/tool-surface changes to @eshyra/core's orchestrator and character systems — explicitly out of scope for the SRD importer/audit epic eshyra-o9bd.18.7.8, which only classifies and tracks them. Recommended implementation order per the artifact: F1+F9 -> F6 -> F2 -> F4 -> F10 -> F7 -> F5 -> F3 -> F8.

*** CLOSURE UNDER RECONCILIATION (2026-07-25) ***
Do NOT cite this epic's closed status as proof of engine completeness. The
2026-07-24 multi-model SRD audit found 794 engine-pending magic-item clauses in
the committed pack three days after this epic closed.

Two things must be checked before relying on any claim here:
  * TAXONOMY. This epic's F1-F10 are NOT the pack's engine:F1-F10
    (data.executionReadiness.clauses[].engineHooks[].engine). This epic used
    F1 dice-grammar, F4 spell-slot economy, F8 character-build gap closures,
    F9 derived-math primitives, F10 currency surface. Only F2/F3/F5/F7 roughly
    correspond. A same-numbered child here does NOT cover the same-numbered pack
    capability family.
  * RECONCILIATION. eshyra-o9bd.19.5.1 owns a required deliverable classifying
    each bead here as: different scope/taxonomy | stale readiness mapping |
    incomplete integration | premature closure. This epic stays closed where the
    scope was genuinely different; individual children reopen only where their
    stated acceptance was objectively unmet.

Engine implementation now continues under eshyra-olc5.
